projectTitle: AmpliRen - a urine-based home screening kit concept for chronic kidney disease using urinary miRNA and hybridisation chain reaction
tagline: Early signals. Made visible. A small sample telling a bigger story.
summary: HongKong-HS is a five-school joint team (Wah Yan College Kowloon, Pope Paul VI College, C&MA Sun Kei Secondary School, Tsung Tsin Christian Academy, St. Paul's School Lam Tin) tackling chronic kidney disease, which affects roughly 788 million adults worldwide, has risen past 405,000 recorded adult cases in Hong Kong, and is usually caught only at stage 3-5 because creatinine-based eGFR does not move until about half of kidney function is gone. AmpliRen detects two urinary microRNAs - miR-21-5p for fibrosis severity and miR-192-5p as an early warning, together reported at 89% sensitivity and 82% specificity - and amplifies the signal enzyme-free at room temperature with hybridisation chain reaction, whose G-rich hairpin loops fold into G-quadruplexes that bind hemin to form a DNAzyme and oxidise TMB into a colour change visible in natural light. The project is a genuine four-cycle engineering story: the team started with toehold switches designed in miRADAR and screened in NUPACK, found EGFP output too weak and invisible, pivoted to HCR, then to G-quadruplex-containing probes, then to hemin/TMB colorimetry. It was nominated for Best Wiki on one of the most ambitious scroll-driven, 3D-visualised wikis in the competition.
awards: Nominee: Best Village Project (Infectious Diseases / Therapeutics / Diagnostics / Oncology)

dry.frameworks: The dry lab is nucleic-acid thermodynamics rather than protein design, and it is used as a hard screen at every cycle. Candidate toehold switches were generated with miRADAR, the design tool released by the 2024 Wageningen iGEM team - a deliberate reuse of another team's software rather than reinventing it - producing 9 candidates for miR-21-5p and 7 for miR-192-5p. Every candidate was then simulated in NUPACK (RNA mode, 37 C, default model options and algorithm settings, 1 uM toehold and 3 uM miRNA to keep the trigger in excess) and scored against five explicit criteria: bound-toehold equilibrium concentration, absence of unintended secondary structure downstream of the ribosome binding site (which would block the ribosome and cause false negatives), hybrid minimum free energy (HMFE) versus toehold minimum free energy (TMFE) so that the bound state is thermodynamically favoured and the switch does not prefer to dimerise with another switch, C-G content for hairpin stability, and RBS location. They tabulated the HMFE-TMFE difference for every candidate in kcal/mol and read NUPACK's base-pair equilibrium-probability plots to check that loop-maintaining base pairs drop to low probability on target binding so the switch can fully linearise - selecting toeholds 6 and 7 for miR-192-5p and 7 and 9 for miR-21-5p. The same NUPACK workflow was then reapplied to HCR: H1/H2 hairpin pairs (the miR-21-5p pair adopted from Miao et al. 2016, the miR-192-5p pair built in house) were simulated at 37 C with 1 uM hairpin and 3 uM miRNA, confirming long H1-H2 polymer formation with target but also predicting unintended H1-H2 binding in the absence of target - a background-leakage problem the model found before the gel did. Minimum-free-energy structures were computed for H1 alone, H2 alone, H1+miRNA and the full miRNA-H1-H2 complex for both targets. In Cycle 4, double-loop G4H1/G4H2 hairpins based on Peng et al. (2022) had InG4 G-quadruplex motifs inserted into the loops, and NUPACK was used to confirm both complex formation and that the InG4 sequences sit in the loops where they can fold and leave the polymer after HCR. The two probe pairs were deliberately given different geometries - longer stems and smaller loops for miR-192-5p, shorter stems and larger loops for miR-21-5p.
dry.dataviz: The wiki itself is the data-visualisation achievement and is why it was nominated for Best Wiki. The landing page is a scroll-driven narrative that zooms from two kidneys, through tissue and the filtration barrier, down to the molecular signal, with each stage labelled as an illustrative view rather than clinical eGFR categories. The HCR mechanism is animated across four scroll states - two locked hairpins, target binding and toehold opening, chain growth into a double-stranded nanowire, then potassium-dependent G-quadruplex folding with hemin - so a reader physically watches the amplification cascade instead of reading a paragraph about it. Epidemiology is presented as individually sourced stat cards, each carrying its own population, year and citation (788 million adults globally, GBD 2023/The Lancet 2025; 87% unaware, CDC 2026 NHANES 2021-2023; 405,833 Hong Kong adult cases 2021, Yue et al.; 2,571 on the transplant waiting list; 1,226 registered deaths in 2024) with an explicit note that one figure is a recorded-case count, not a current population estimate. The kit concept is presented as an interactive unboxing with three fitted compartments and a pannable close-up, and the team labels it openly as AI-assisted imagery and animation made with Higgsfield and as a research concept, not a validated diagnostic product. The engineering page is built as a clickable 22-note timeline across four Design-Build-Test-Learn cycles. Every figure carries a full descriptive caption and alt text.
dry.datascience: Analysis is modest in volume but correctly specified. Cell-free EGFP expression was compared with and without target miRNA across five repeats against both positive controls (pET-14b-EGFP with no toehold) and no-plasmid negative controls, read on a fluorometer at 488 nm excitation and 507-513 nm emission, with significance tested by one-sample t-test on fold change; the honest outcome was that miR-21 candidates showed no significant difference, miR-192-5p-6 was significant but minimal at 1.03-fold, and miR-192-5p-7 showed a more pronounced 1.51-fold increase that did not reach significance - and they reported that rather than spin it. ThT fluorescence and hemin/TMB colorimetric assays were analysed by one-way ANOVA with Dunnett post-hoc against the 0 pM control: miR-21 gave significant signal at 100 pM, 10 nM and 100 nM (n=3, p<0.001), while miR-192 was significant at 100 nM (p=0.01 and p=0.002) but also, unexpectedly, significantly lower than control at 1 nM - an anomaly they diagnosed as free miR-192-5p G4H1 self-folding into a G-quadruplex and producing colour without target, and then turned into a concrete future-work list (splitting the G4, stabilising the hairpin stem, tuning C-G/A-T content, optimising toehold length). Plasmid work was confirmed by Sanger sequencing and miniprep A260/280 purity, and gel evidence was escalated from agarose to PAGE when agarose smearing proved inconclusive.
dry.software: No standalone software or hardware was released. The dry lab is the application of existing tools - NUPACK for thermodynamic simulation and another iGEM team's miRADAR for candidate generation - plus a bespoke wiki front end. Two toehold switch candidates per target were cloned into pET-14b-EGFP using XbaI and NdeI sites between the T7 promoter and the EGFP reporter and verified by Sanger sequencing, and an mCherry colorimetric variant was in progress when the season ended.
techniques: HMFE vs TMFE thermodynamic ranking of toehold candidates
equilibrium base-pair probability inspection to verify hairpin linearisation on target binding
in-silico prediction of background leakage (unintended H1-H2 binding without target) before bench testing
MFE structure comparison across free hairpin, hairpin+target and full ternary complex
loop-position verification for inserted G-quadruplex motifs
fold-change analysis against both positive and no-plasmid negative controls
escalating gel resolution (agarose to PAGE) when a result is inconclusive
diagnosing a statistically anomalous result as probe self-folding and converting it into a redesign list

good.publicEngagement: Education reached over 800 participants and was built on three stated principles - a Cascading Peer-Educator Model, Gamified Educational Experiences, and Reflective Learning. The peer-educator model is the distinctive one: rather than only teaching end-learners, they trained non-iGEM junior-form Science Team members as Student Facilitators with both content and facilitation skills, then had those facilitators independently run workshops for their schoolmates, and published a training guide for holding a secondary school workshop plus a CKD brochure for older adults so the materials outlive the team. Activities were designed per audience and deliberately low-cost and replicable: at Salesian Yip Hon Millennium Primary School's STEAM Day (about 600 students and parents) they ran a micropipette drip-art station, a magnetic miRNA detection game in which only the target miRNA card hides a magnet so it alone sticks to a paper toehold-switch model, and a health-knowledge ping-pong ball toss into an illustrated face; at Shek Lei Catholic Primary School, strawberry DNA extraction delivered entirely in Cantonese with terms simplified ('cell walls' became 'the surface of the strawberry') and a 'Blood Vessel Clearing Game' using paper, drawing supplies and a hand-made wooden vessel model, with students drawing their own food items and testing whether they fit through. Secondary outreach covered St. Paul's School (Lam Tin) with 169 participants and Hoi Ping Chamber of Commerce Secondary School with 19, using a micropipetting precision-dyeing challenge and a 'Detective on Call' online DNA fingerprinting game. They also ran a card game for community-centre children including ethnic-minority children, an elderly workshop, a Hong Kong Joint Secondary Schools Science Fair booth, and regional middle-school outreach in the Greater Bay Area. Reflection was built in with structured worksheets, exit cards and open Q&A, and every activity records what they changed next - after noticing their terminology was too advanced for young children they switched to plainer language, more gestures and more Cantonese, and they adapted in real time when a student asked 'Why strawberries? Why not apples?' by adding an impromptu discussion.
good.ihp: IHP was organised as four parallel two-way feedback loops (Public, Healthcare, Science, Industry) feeding both the wet lab and the education team, structured over three stages (Understanding the Problem, Identifying the Needs, Develop & Co-design) and processed through a four-step cycle they call LIVP (Locate, Iterate, Validate, Propose). The design changes are traceable to named people. Professor Chan Ting Fung (RNA biology) assessed the toehold-switch limitations and identified HCR as the alternative worth trying for signal amplification - the single biggest pivot in the project - and later recommended expanding the H1/H2 sequence design space to mask the ribosome binding site to eliminate background leakage, noted that lithium interference in urine is negligible, and told them to test sodium's effect on the DNAzyme experimentally. Professor Szeto Cheuk Chun (Head of Medicine and Therapeutics, CUHK, whose research is urinary biomarkers) confirmed miRNA as near-ideal for urine because of its stability, told them to run miR-21-5p and miR-192-5p in parallel as a complementary test (which is why the kit has two detection pathways and a six-well chamber), said biomarkers are detectable in urine that has not been high-speed centrifuged so they could drop centrifugation from the workflow, warned that urinary chromogens may interfere with a visible colour readout, set a user-experience target of roughly half an hour to result, and endorsed a colour change readable under natural light - which is precisely why the team ended up on G4/hemin colorimetry rather than ThT fluorescence, since ThT needs UV excitation and a fluorescence reader. Professor Ma Ming Yao established that the kit must be positioned as a screening flag prompting medical follow-up, never a diagnosis, and that false positives and negatives must be managed responsibly, and that high-risk patients are the target - which reshaped how the whole wiki speaks about the product and prompted a community education workshop for the elderly. A medical laboratory technologist insisted on a clear, reasonable cut-off concentration for the target miRNA, rigorous quality control, timely sample processing, and a larger sample size for credibility, which pushed the team towards a multi-target design. E-SENSE Innovation & Technology Limited said clinicians will only recommend a home test backed by real-world clinical data with low false-positive and false-negative rates, which pushed the wet lab to run the cell-free EGFP validation and the HCR sensitivity series. Public input was quantified: a street interview of 137 people and an online survey of 283 found 52% had never heard of CKD or diabetic kidney disease and only 28% had heard of both, 60% did not know or were unsure that early kidney disease can be symptomless, and 63.2% of street respondents cited absence of symptoms as their reason for not getting screened.
good.realWorld: The intended product is an at-home urine screening kit, costed against a system where each Hong Kong dialysis patient runs about HKD 50,000 per year and where confirming CKD currently needs repeat clinic visits over a three-month window because uACR varies by 30% or more day to day and cystatin C is several times the price of creatinine and rarely reimbursed. Every design decision is pulled towards deployability: urine rather than blood, no centrifuge, enzyme-free isothermal amplification at room temperature, and a colour change readable in natural light without any instrument. The team is consistently careful about regulatory and clinical positioning - the kit is repeatedly described as a screening flag that prompts follow-up and complements, rather than replaces, eGFR and uACR, and the kit visualisation is explicitly captioned as a research concept, not a validated diagnostic product. What is not present on the wiki is a business model, pricing, manufacturing plan or named regulatory pathway; industry engagement with E-SENSE is framed around clinical credibility and usability requirements rather than commercialisation, and the honest gap they name is the need for real-world paired clinical data before a home device is justified.

gemsTakeaway: Two things to steal. First, NUPACK plus a reused iGEM software tool (Wageningen's miRADAR) is a complete, free, high-school-feasible dry lab: HongKong-HS ranked 16 candidate switches on explicit thermodynamic criteria (HMFE vs TMFE, downstream secondary structure blocking the RBS, equilibrium base-pair probability) and predicted the background-leakage failure mode before the gel showed it. Second, their wiki proves that the best data visualisation is mechanism animation plus per-figure provenance - every statistic carries its own population, year and source, and the AI-generated product imagery is labelled as such, which is exactly the standard a research centre's outputs should hold itself to.
